name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area composite PMI was 51.7 in October, a four-month low but above 50; growth stays positive
state: The HCOB euro-area composite PMI came in at 51.7 in October, below the 51.9 expected, as business activity growth slowed to a four-month low (FXStreet, 4 Nov; Trading Economics). With the index above 50 and no technical recession or ECB action against bond-spread fragmentation found as of 26 Nov, the signal stays Normal, although French activity is weakening.
for_you: Euro-area firms are still expanding, though more slowly; jobs and exporters tied to European demand face a softer outlook.
rubric_hit: Composite PMI 51.7 > 50 with positive growth = Normal

sources.title: FXStreet — Eurozone HCOB Composite PMI registered at 51.7, below expectations, in October
Trading Economics — Eurozone business activity slows in October

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
